answer: Fingerprint Anchor Costing. Each new identity must store a unique device-level anchor—a composite hardware and timing fingerprint—in a shared append-only ledger; duplicates or near-matches are rejected at write time, so each identity needs distinct physical hardware. The ledger grows like a garden, and every entry costs the attacker a fresh device plus a recurring audit fee proportional to how similar its fingerprint pigment is to existing entries. Closer imitation pays more, making mass fabrication linearly expensive per identity.
